rubric.description: Expands DoS as Denial of Service.
rubric.how: Award for correctly stating the expansion.

rubric.why: Explains the purpose or effect of the attack.
rubric.description: States that the attack overwhelms a system or network so its services become unavailable to users.
rubric.how: Award for describing the disruption or unavailability of services.

modelAnswer: A DoS (Denial of Service) attack overwhelms a computer or network with requests.
This makes its services unavailable to legitimate users.

rubric.why: Identifies ciphertext as the result of encryption.
rubric.description: States that cipher text is an encrypted message or text.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as encrypted information.

rubric.why: Explains how the text appears without decryption.
rubric.description: States that it cannot be understood without decryption.
rubric.how: Award for describing its unreadable or unintelligible form.

modelAnswer: Cipher text is the encrypted form of a message.
It cannot be understood unless it is decrypted.

items.followUp: Give an example of a multipoint connection.

rubric.why: Identifies the devices involved in the example.
rubric.how: Award for specifying two connected devices.

rubric.why: Shows that the connection is a direct link between the two devices.
rubric.description: Gives a direct connection example, such as two computers linked by a cable.
rubric.how: Award for a valid point-to-point example.

modelAnswer: An example is two computers connected directly to each other by a cable.

items.followUp: How does a client-server system handle a request from a client?

rubric.description: States that a client sends a request to the server.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the client request.

rubric.description: States that the server processes the request and sends a response or data back.
rubric.how: Award for explaining the server's response.

modelAnswer: A client sends a request for data or a service to the server.
The server processes the request and sends a response to the client.

items.followUp: What is the use of HTTP?

rubric.description: Expands FTP as File Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award for correctly stating the protocol's name.

rubric.why: States what FTP is used for.
rubric.description: Explains that FTP transfers files between computers over a network.

modelAnswer: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.
It is used to transfer files between computers over a network.

items.followUp: What is the function of a switch in a network?

rubric.why: Identifies the hub's role in a network.
rubric.description: States that a hub is a central device used to connect computers or other devices in a network.
rubric.how: Award for describing its central connecting role.

rubric.why: Explains how a hub sends data.
rubric.description: States that a hub broadcasts received data to all its ports or connected devices.
rubric.how: Award for noting that data is sent to all connected devices.

modelAnswer: A hub is a central device that connects computers in a network.
It broadcasts received data to all its ports.

items.followUp: Write one difference between an ordered list and a table in HTML.

rubric.why: States how an ordered list displays its items.
rubric.description: States that an ordered list displays items in a numbered or otherwise ordered sequence.
rubric.how: Award for identifying numbering or sequence.

rubric.why: States how an unordered list displays its items.
rubric.description: States that an unordered list displays items with bullets and no numbered sequence.
rubric.how: Award for identifying bullets or the absence of numbering.

modelAnswer: An ordered list uses the <ol> tag and displays its items in a numbered sequence.
An unordered list uses the <ul> tag and displays its items with bullets.

items.followUp: Write the output of HTML code that has the title “My Page” and the body paragraph “Hello World.”

rubric.why: Identifies the text specified in the HTML title element.
rubric.description: States that “welcome” appears as the page title, usually in the browser title bar or tab.
rubric.how: Award for giving the title text.

rubric.why: Identifies the text displayed in the body.
rubric.description: States that “I Love Pakistan” is displayed on the webpage.
rubric.how: Award for giving the body output.

modelAnswer: The browser tab or title bar shows: welcome
The webpage displays: I Love Pakistan
